meta.name: lineage
meta.description: Language-neutral expected verifier outcomes for the lineage declaration (spec/lineage.md, `manifest.predecessors`). PRESENCE BINDS, ABSENCE REPORTS: an absent member is 'no claim' (declared=false, reported); a PRESENT malformed declaration is the capsule asserting something meaningless about its own origin and fails closed with the shared `predecessors[i].<member>` diagnoses. Identity coherence is era-keyed and SKIPPED (identity_checked=false, never failed) for unknown declared eras. Linkage against a supplied predecessor pool (per-vector `predecessors`, paths relative to this file) is REPORT-ONLY: it can falsify the lineage AREA (`expected.lineage.ok`) but never the capsule's overall ok — the ok-true-under-mismatch vectors pin that a host's file handling cannot flip a valid capsule's verdict, and no lane may 'helpfully' harden this into a parity break. Entry statuses are the closed vocabulary unverified | verified | mismatch | predecessor_invalid | predecessor_unverifiable (reason: unsupported_version | encrypted_predecessor | unsupported_profile | unsupported_capability). v0.7.1 declarations commit to plain, DEFAULT-PROFILE (v0.6-suite) predecessors; encrypted and alternate-profile supplies report predecessor_unverifiable with the scope reason — a verifier/scope limitation, never mismatch, never predecessor_invalid. Any unchecked entry MUST render with 'declared, not verified', and declared lineage MUST render with 'not countersigned' — a citation must never launder into an endorsement. expected.qualifiers pins the emitted lineage qualifier names exactly (bare strings, non-empty only on a valid verdict; payload-carrying facts live in the lineage area).
meta.no_warranty: Conformance fixtures only; not production templates or advice.

vectors.name: no-lineage-control
vectors.note: Positive control: no predecessors member. No claim, nothing checked, declared=false reported. Absence is a weaker claim made honestly — never a failure, never a qualifier.

vectors.name: declared-unverified
vectors.note: Declared lineage with no predecessor bytes supplied. The entry MUST be reported (never omitted) with the pinned phrase 'declared, not verified', and the report MUST state the declaration is one-way ('not countersigned'). The lineage_declared_unverified qualifier is EMITTED in v0.7.1, not reserved.

vectors.name: linkage-verified-depth-1
vectors.note: The F-03 hand-off, verified: Bob's successor + Alice's exact sealed artifact. All six equalities hold against RECOMPUTED values (id under the predecessor's era domain, manifest_hash from stored bytes — never the artifact's own claims). The verified report presents two distinct identities; the successor is never presented as BEING the predecessor.

vectors.name: linkage-verified-depth-2
vectors.note: Era-keyed recursive walk: after Bob's capsule verifies, ITS first-person declaration joins the frontier and matches Alice's artifact at hop 2 — no hop is hearsay. Carol's manifest declares exactly ONE entry (re-rewrap never accumulates an inline ancestry list); deep ancestry is recovered hop by hop from supplied bytes.

vectors.name: merge-two-predecessors
vectors.note: A merge declares one entry per immediate parent, each an independent claim verified independently. One branch supplied: verified + unverified, verified_depth stays 0 (depth counts only when EVERY declared entry within the hop is verified). An operator legitimately holds one branch of a merge — the unsupplied entry is reported, never an exit-policy failure.

vectors.name: unendorsed-successor-verifies
vectors.note: THE checked-in honest reading of the reputation-squat non-defense: a DIFFERENT, unaffiliated key seals a successor of someone else's public capsule and everything verifies. Prevention is impossible in this artifact class without the predecessor's key endorsing the successor (the v0.8+ countersignature artifact); the format converts the squat into an exact, attributable, non-exclusive, signed claim. The two pinned ids are distinct — the successor squats on nothing — and the required 'not countersigned' language keeps citation from laundering into endorsement. No lane may 'fix' this vector.

vectors.name: lineage-from-v06-predecessor
vectors.note: Cross-era citation is a feature: the declaration names format_version 0.6, standalone identity coherence recomputes under capsule-id-v0.6 (the era-keyed domain discipline every verifier already retains forever), and linkage verifies the predecessor under the v0.6 rules. The fixture is a BYTE-IDENTICAL copy of version-compat/output/known-previous-version-0.6.capsule — frozen, never regenerated, never resealed; the generator's --check asserts byte equality with the original.

vectors.name: zero-event-predecessor
vectors.note: A template hand-off: the predecessor is a sealed ZERO-EVENT capsule, so the entry declares first_event_hash and entry_hash both null (the empty-chain anchor rule applied to a reference) and identity coherence uses 32 zero bytes in place of the first event hash — the same genesis stand-in as the capsule_id derivation.

vectors.name: same-id-zero-event-rewrap
vectors.note: Pins the deliberate ABSENCE of a self-reference rule: a same-key zero-event template rewrap honestly declares a predecessor id EQUAL to its own id (two zero-event capsules from one originator share a capsule_id — id equality is not artifact identity). A lane that adds a self-reference rejection brands this legitimate corner a lie. The true self-reference (declared manifest_hash equal to the capsule's own) is a hash fixpoint and cannot be constructed.

vectors.name: member-not-array
vectors.note: A present declaration no reader can interpret is the capsule asserting something meaningless about its own origin — fail closed with the same diagnosis in every lane, never a lane-specific parse crash (typed lanes parse leniently and diagnose at check time).

vectors.name: empty-array
vectors.note: 'No claim' has exactly one spelling: absence (the present-but-empty signer_commitment precedent).

vectors.name: entry-missing-manifest-hash
vectors.note: All six entry members are REQUIRED: there is no weaker declaration made honestly INSIDE an entry — the weaker honest claim is the member's absence plus prose in program.md.

vectors.name: bad-hex-uppercase
vectors.note: Lowercase is REQUIRED, not normalized: the claim is bound by its stored bytes, and case-variant spellings of one claim are a cross-lane comparison differential.

vectors.name: version-grammar-violation
vectors.note: format_version follows the versioning.md <major>.<minor> grammar; 'v0.7' is a malformed declaration, not an unknown era.

vectors.name: duplicate-manifest-hash
vectors.note: Two entries sharing a manifest_hash cite the same sealed artifact twice — no legitimate producer, exists only to create counting differentials (the duplicate-signer precedent). Two entries sharing capsule_id with DIFFERENT manifest_hash values remain legal (a merge of two snapshots of one line).

vectors.name: null-incoherent
vectors.note: first_event_hash null with entry_hash 64-hex describes a predecessor that cannot exist — the empty-chain anchor rule applied to a reference.

vectors.name: id-not-derivable
vectors.note: Identity coherence under a KNOWN declared era: the declared capsule_id must equal the recompute under that era's identity rule. No honest writer produces a mismatch (writers derive from predecessor bytes); no external evidence is involved, so this is self-assertion, not linkage — fail closed.

vectors.name: era-unknown-declared
vectors.note: A well-formed declaration naming era 0.9: versioning.md forbids applying one era's identity formula to another era's claim, so the recompute is SKIPPED and reported (identity_checked=false), never failed. The successor is not lying; this verifier is too old for the declared predecessor's era — the unknown-era skip is the malleability release valve. The SUCCESSOR itself is a 0.7 capsule and its verdict stays valid.

vectors.name: mismatch-different-seal
vectors.note: THE anti-framing pin: the supplied file is a LATER genuine seal of the same line (same key, same genesis, one more event — same capsule_id, different sealed state). The entry reports mismatch with the pinned phrase 'different sealed state of the declared predecessor', the wording never uses tamper/corruption vocabulary (the honest cause is the host's own file handling), and the capsule's overall ok stays TRUE — linkage is report-only, so a hostile host cannot flip a valid capsule's verdict by supplying the wrong file. A lane that hardens this into overall failure is non-conforming.

vectors.name: predecessor-fails-own-verification
vectors.note: The two-fact split, never collapsed: the supplied artifact IS the declared artifact (its manifest matches the declared manifest_hash) AND it fails its own verification (a flipped content byte). Status predecessor_invalid takes precedence over mismatch; the diagnosis is a property of the supplied artifact under its own era, distinct from any claim about the successor's honesty. Overall ok stays true — report-only.

vectors.name: encrypted-predecessor-unverifiable
vectors.note: Plain-predecessor scope: v0.7.1 defines no mapping from a declaration onto an encrypted capsule's outer/inner manifest pair, so an encrypted supply is reported predecessor_unverifiable/encrypted_predecessor — never guessed at, never mismatch. The genuine encrypted use case needs no special case: decrypt the inner (which IS a plain capsule) and supply it. Lanes without an encryption path map this to their documented plain-only refusal per the registry consumer notes.

vectors.name: predecessor-unsupported-profile
vectors.note: Default-profile scope (the lineage × profile composition rule): v0.7.1 declarations commit to default-profile (v0.6-suite) predecessors — the entry grammar presumes the era-default identity derivation and key encoding. A supplied predecessor declaring a profile this verifier does not implement reports predecessor_unverifiable/unsupported_profile: a verifier/scope limitation, NEVER mismatch and NEVER predecessor_invalid — branding an honest alternate-profile citation a defect is the slander the profile diagnosis discipline exists to kill.

vectors.name: inner-outer-mismatch
vectors.note: Encrypted successor whose inner and outer manifests BOTH declare predecessors with different values. Each layer alone is well-formed, so L2 (outer) verifies; L3 fails closed on the inner/outer JCS byte inequality — a capsule asserting one origin to the world and another to its recipients is lying about itself across layers. Single-layer placement (inner-only private citation, outer-only public citation) stays legal: each is a weaker claim made honestly, and mandating symmetry would force disclosure of a confidential association.

vectors.name: tampered-predecessors-member
vectors.note: Post-seal mutation of one declared member (a hex digit of predecessors[0].manifest_hash): the declaration is ordinary manifest content inside the JCS bytes of manifest_hash, under every signature — so the recomputed manifest hash diverges from the envelope's signed claim and verification fails. A third party cannot redirect a sealed successor's lineage; a false citation is a SIGNED false citation, permanently pinned to its author's key.
